# API Contracts — apps/web

*Generated by the BMad document-project workflow — deep scan, 2026-07-17.*

## Overview

`apps/web` exposes its entire HTTP surface as Next.js App Router route handlers under [`apps/web/app/api/**`](../apps/web/app/api). There is **no `pages/api`** directory and **no `"use server"` server action** anywhere in the tree (verified: `grep -rl '"use server"' apps/web` returns nothing). All mutation and read paths are `route.ts` files.

Scale (re-counted directly against the tree, not taken from prior scan findings): **56 `route.ts` files**, **70 exported HTTP method handlers** (33 `GET`, 27 `POST`, 7 `DELETE`, 3 `PATCH`, 0 `PUT`). 55 of the 56 route files set `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"`; the sole exception is [`apps/web/app/api/chat/route.ts`](../apps/web/app/api/chat/route.ts) (verified: `grep -n "dynamic" apps/web/app/api/chat/route.ts` returns zero matches).

**No authentication/authorization layer exists.** There is no `middleware.ts` anywhere in `apps/web`, no session cookie, no API key check, on any route — every handler trusts the local caller unconditionally. This matches the product shape: Telar's web app is a local, single-operator cockpit (see [`../apps/desktop`](../apps/desktop) for the Electron shell that boots it). The only "auth" concepts in this surface are **provider login** (Claude/Codex account credentials, `apps/web/app/api/accounts/[name]/login/route.ts`) and **MCP OAuth** (`apps/web/app/api/mcp/oauth/**`) — both are about authenticating *outbound* calls to third-party services, not about authenticating the caller of these routes.

Response conventions:
- Success bodies are `Response.json({...})`; a few static-file and diagnostic routes return raw `Response`/`Response.json` with plain-text bodies.
- Error bodies are `{ error: string }`, occasionally extended (`{ error, needsClientId: true }` on `POST /api/mcp/oauth/connect`; `{ ok: false }` as a soft-failure signal on permission/watch-cancel routes).
- Status codes are hand-chosen per route: `400` (validation), `404` (not found), `409` (conflict — already logged in, already resolved, stale concurrent edit), `422` (actionable client-side follow-up needed), `500`/`502` (upstream/process failure). A handful of routes are deliberately **fail-open** and never return 5xx — the `git/remote/**` family degrades to `{connected:false, reason:"gh-error"}` on any throw so the UI panel degrades gracefully instead of erroring.
- All business logic is delegated to [`@telar/core`](../packages/core/src/index.ts) (loom engine, project/account registries, MCP OAuth, policy) or to `apps/web/lib/*` helpers that wrap file-backed local state (`store.ts`, `chat-runs.ts`, `session-log.ts`, `permissions.ts`, `server/git-tab.ts`).

Every endpoint below was verified by reading its route file directly (not solely from prior scan output); where a prior finding disagreed with the code, the code's behavior is what's documented (see "Endpoint Summary" note on handler count).

## Endpoint Contracts

### Accounts

#### `GET /api/accounts`
File: [`apps/web/app/api/accounts/route.ts`](../apps/web/app/api/accounts/route.ts)
- No params. Lists every registered account, each enriched with on-disk `accountHealth`.
- Response: `{ accounts: (AccountProfile & { health })[], default: string }`.
- Core: `listAccounts`, `accountHealth`, `getDefaultAccountName`.

#### `POST /api/accounts`
File: same as above.
- Body: an `AccountProfile` object, validated via `AccountProfile.safeParse` (zod, from `@telar/core`). `name` restricted to `/^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$/`.
- `400` on schema failure or invalid name characters. Response `{ account }`.
- Core: `upsertAccount`, `AccountProfile` schema.

#### `PATCH /api/accounts/[name]`
File: [`apps/web/app/api/accounts/[name]/route.ts`](../apps/web/app/api/accounts/[name]/route.ts)
- Body: `{ makeDefault: true }`. `404` if the account is unknown.
- Core: `setDefaultAccount`.

#### `DELETE /api/accounts/[name]`
File: same as above.
- Removes the registry entry and stored token; leaves the on-disk config directory untouched. Response `{ ok: boolean }`.
- Core: `removeAccount`.

#### `GET /api/accounts/[name]/login`
File: [`apps/web/app/api/accounts/[name]/login/route.ts`](../apps/web/app/api/accounts/[name]/login/route.ts)
- SSE stream that drives the provider login CLI in-process (`spawnProviderLogin`): Codex self-completes, Claude waits for a pasted code delivered via the `POST` below. One in-flight session per account name, tracked in an in-process `Map<string, LoginSession>` — a new login for the same name supersedes and kills the old one.
- `404` unknown account; `409` if `accountHealth(account).status === "ok"` (already logged in).
- Emits whatever `session.events` (from `@telar/core`'s `spawnProviderLogin`) yields, plus a synthetic `{ type: "failed", error }` on throw. **Note:** unlike every other SSE route in this app, this one writes bare `data: <json>\n\n` frames with no `event:` field — see "Streaming Protocols" below.
- Core: `accountHealth`, `getAccount`, `spawnProviderLogin`, `LoginSession` type.

#### `POST /api/accounts/[name]/login`
File: same as above.
- Body: `{ code: string }` submits the pasted OAuth code to the in-flight session (`session.submitCode`), **or** `{ terminal: true }` hands off to a real macOS `Terminal.app` window via `osascript` (spawns `claude`/`codex` login command with the account's config-dir env prefix).
- `404` unknown account; `409` if `{code}` sent but no session is in progress; `400` if the body matches neither shape.
- Core: `providerOf`, `loginCommand` (used only by the `terminal` branch).

#### `DELETE /api/accounts/[name]/login`
File: same as above.
- Cancels an in-flight login session unconditionally (no-op if none). Response `{ ok: true }`.

### Filesystem browse

#### `POST /api/browse`
File: [`apps/web/app/api/browse/route.ts`](../apps/web/app/api/browse/route.ts)
- macOS-only native Finder folder picker via `osascript`; other platforms get `501`. No body. Response `{ path }` or `{ cancelled: true }`.
- Core: none (OS-level only).

### Chat (agent turn engine)

#### `POST /api/chat`
File: [`apps/web/app/api/chat/route.ts`](../apps/web/app/api/chat/route.ts) — 1909 lines, the largest and most complex route in the app.

Runs **one agent turn** — via the Claude Agent SDK's `query()`, or (for Codex-provider accounts) `runCodexTurn` from `apps/web/lib/codex-app-server` — and streams the full interaction back as SSE, persisting the turn at teardown regardless of client disconnect.

**Request body** (JSON):

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `message` | string | The user turn (or the escalation-kickoff sentinel, resolved server-side). |
| `sessionId` | string? | Resume target. |
| `model` | string? | |
| `project` | string | **Required.** Resolved via `getProject`; `400` if unknown. |
| `account` | string? | Resolved via `getAccount`; `400` if unknown; falls back to the project manifest's account (`400` if that account isn't registered locally). |
| `effort` | string? | Validated against `EFFORT_OPTIONS` (Claude) or `CODEX_EFFORT_OPTIONS`/inline `CODEX_EFFORT_LEVELS` (Codex); `400` if present but invalid. |
| `permissionMode` | `"default"\|"auto"\|"acceptEdits"` | Default `"default"`. `isValidPermissionMode` **rejects** `"bypassPermissions"`, `"dontAsk"`, `"plan"` regardless of what the client sends — `400` otherwise. |
| `sandbox` | string? | Codex only; validated against `CODEX_SANDBOX_PRESETS`/inline `CODEX_SANDBOXES`. |
| `approvalPolicy` | `"untrusted"\|"on-request"\|"never"` | Codex only; defaults `"on-request"`. |
| `role` | `"planner"\|"steerer"\|"escalation"` | Anything else collapses to `undefined` (fail-safe). |
| `loomId` | string? | Turn-1 seed linking a `steerer` session to a loom; validated against `getLoom` + project match before trust. |
| `runId` | string? | Client-generated turn id for `POST /api/chat/stop` targeting; server mints a UUID if omitted. |
| `ultra` | boolean? | Per-message Ultra-chip annotation; only a literal `true` is honored. |

Validation order (each a plain `400`, before any stream opens): project → account → account health (`missing-config-dir`/`never-logged-in` → `400` with a login-hint command string) → effort → sandbox/approvalPolicy (Codex only) → permissionMode.

**Response**: `text/event-stream`. Named SSE events (verified via every `send(event, ...)` call site): `session`, `saved`, `thinking`, `thinking_delta`, `delta`, `text`, `tool`, `tool_result`, `task_status`, `permission`, `permission_result`, `permission_denied`, `plan`, `error`, `interrupted`, `done`, `title` — 17 distinct event types.

Selected payload shapes (read from source, not inferred):
- `session` — `{ sessionId, slashCommands, skills, agents }`, sent on SDK `system:init`.
- `saved` — `{ chatId }`, sent once at register-at-create (a stub chat row is persisted the instant the session id is known, via `upsertChatStub`) and again after final persistence.
- `permission` — `{ id, toolName, input, rule, ruleOptions }` for an interactive `canUseTool` prompt; answered by `POST /api/chat/permission`.
- `permission_result` — `{ id, behavior }`.
- `done` — `{ subtype, costUsd, turns, usage, context }`, the terminal per-POST summary (`context` is real final context-window occupancy, not a running sum).
- `title` — `{ title }`, sent only if a background title-generation job (`generateTitle`) resolves within `TITLE_RACE_MS`.

**Human-accept moat enforced at this layer**: `mcp__loom__start_loom` and `mcp__loom__answer_blocked` (`LOOM_START_TOOL`, `LOOM_ANSWER_BLOCKED_TOOL`) are force-routed through the interactive `canUseTool` card **in every permission mode**, including `auto`/`acceptEdits` — the stored-"always allow"-rules fast path is explicitly skipped for these two tool names (`readRules(project).some(...)` guard excludes them), and `decision.always` is never persisted for them either. `AskUserQuestion` is hard-disallowed. Guardrails (`makeGuardrailDecision`, `manifest.guardrails.disallowedTools`, protected paths) are applied via both the `canUseTool` callback and a `PreToolUse` hook (belt-and-suspenders against an `auto`/`acceptEdits` bypass).

In-process MCP servers wired per turn: `loom` (`createLoomMcpServer`, from [`apps/web/lib/loom-mcp.ts`](../apps/web/lib/loom-mcp.ts) — 13 tools: `draft_bundle_file`, `propose_contract`, `read_bundle`, `list_looms`, `get_loom`, `start_loom`, `steer_loom`, `reject_loom`, `answer_loom`, `answer_blocked`, `resume_loom`, `cancel_loom`, `watch_loom`), `ultra` (`createUltraMcpServer`, from [`apps/web/lib/ultra-mcp.ts`](../apps/web/lib/ultra-mcp.ts) — `ultra`/`ultra_status`/`ultra_stop`), plus any project-declared MCP servers via `resolveProjectMcpServers` with `strictMcpConfig: true` (the repo's own `.mcp.json`/user-level config is never pulled in).

Persistence at teardown (`finally` block — the turn is not bound to the HTTP request lifetime, so it survives client disconnect): `appendTurn` and `logUsage` (both `apps/web/lib/store.ts`). Background execution is tracked via `registerChatRun(runId, abort)` (`apps/web/lib/chat-runs.ts`) — only `POST /api/chat/stop` or natural completion aborts it.

Core (`@telar/core`): `accountEnv`, `accountHealth`, `deriveDeliverableSignal`, `getAccount`, `getLoom`, `getProject`, `providerOf`, `readBundleFile`, `readContract`, `resolveProjectMcpServers`, `STEERING_FILE`.

#### `GET /api/chat/[sessionId]/events`
File: [`apps/web/app/api/chat/[sessionId]/events/route.ts`](../apps/web/app/api/chat/[sessionId]/events/route.ts)
- Reconnect-tail SSE of a session's **currently in-flight** turn: replays finalized events from an append-only per-session log file (`readSessionEvents`) then the live in-flight block from a bounded delta ring (`readSessionDeltas`), polling every 300ms. Re-emits the **same named events** the `POST /api/chat` stream sent for that turn (not a generic `run`/`ev`/`end` envelope).
- Gated by `isSessionRunLive`: on the very first tick, if the run isn't live (turn already completed and is sitting in `chats.json`), the stream finishes silently with no events — an anti-double-render guard.
- No body. Uses `apps/web/lib/chat-runs.ts` (`isSessionRunLive`) and `apps/web/lib/session-log.ts` (`readSessionDeltas`, `readSessionEvents`, `DeltaCursor` type). No `@telar/core` import.

#### `GET /api/chat/[sessionId]/watches`
File: [`apps/web/app/api/chat/[sessionId]/watches/route.ts`](../apps/web/app/api/chat/[sessionId]/watches/route.ts)
- Lists the session's active loom watches (registered via the `watch_loom` MCP tool). Response `{ watches }`.
- Core: `listWatches`.

#### `DELETE /api/chat/[sessionId]/watches?id=<watchId>`
File: same as above.
- Cancels one watch by id (query param). `400` if `id` missing. Response `{ cancelled: boolean }`.
- Core: `cancelWatch`.

#### `POST /api/chat/permission`
File: [`apps/web/app/api/chat/permission/route.ts`](../apps/web/app/api/chat/permission/route.ts)
- Answers a pending `canUseTool` request opened by an in-flight `/api/chat` stream.
- Body: `{ id: string, behavior: "allow"|"deny", always?: boolean, rule?: string }`. `400` if `id`/`behavior` malformed. If `rule` is present it **must** be exactly one of the options remembered server-side for that pending request (`pendingRuleOptions(id)` + `isOfferedRule`) — a client-supplied rule string that wasn't offered is rejected with `400`; the server never trusts an arbitrary rule string.
- Response `{ ok: boolean }` — `false` means already resolved, timed out, or unknown id.
- Uses `apps/web/lib/permissions.ts` (`resolvePending`, `pendingRuleOptions`, `isOfferedRule`). No `@telar/core` import.

#### `POST /api/chat/stop`
File: [`apps/web/app/api/chat/stop/route.ts`](../apps/web/app/api/chat/stop/route.ts)
- Aborts a background chat turn by `runId` (preferred) or `sessionId` fallback.
- Body `{ runId?, sessionId? }`. `400` if neither present. Response `{ ok: boolean }`.
- Uses `apps/web/lib/chat-runs.ts` (`stopChatRun`).

### Chats (persisted session list)

#### `GET /api/chats?project=&archived=`
File: [`apps/web/app/api/chats/route.ts`](../apps/web/app/api/chats/route.ts)
- Lists regular chat sessions for a project (all projects if `project` omitted). `archived` query: `exclude` (default) | `include` | `only`. Filters out loom-born sessions (`role === "steerer" | "escalation"`) — those are reachable only via `GET /api/looms/[id]/chat`.
- Response `{ chats }`. Uses `apps/web/lib/store.ts` (`listChats`).

#### `GET /api/chats/[id]`
File: [`apps/web/app/api/chats/[id]/route.ts`](../apps/web/app/api/chats/[id]/route.ts)
- Full chat record including transcript. `404` (plain-text `"not found"` body) if missing.
- Uses `getChat`.

#### `PATCH /api/chats/[id]`
File: same as above.
- Rename: `{ title: string }` (1–120 chars, trimmed) → `setChatTitle(id, title, {custom:true})`. **Or** archive toggle: `{ archived: boolean }` → `setChatArchived`. If both are present, title wins. `400` on missing/invalid fields; `404` if chat not found.

#### `DELETE /api/chats/[id]`
File: same as above.
- Deletes the chat. `204 No Content`. Uses `deleteChat`.

### Doctor / diagnostics

#### `GET /api/doctor`
File: [`apps/web/app/api/doctor/route.ts`](../apps/web/app/api/doctor/route.ts)
- Machine-readiness report: driver binaries, GitHub auth, provider account liveness, verifier browser, active `TELAR_HOME`. Read-only, never touches credentials.
- Uses `apps/web/lib/server/doctor.ts` (`runDoctor`) — not `@telar/core` directly.

### Loom (unit-of-work engine)

#### `GET /api/looms`
File: [`apps/web/app/api/looms/route.ts`](../apps/web/app/api/looms/route.ts)
- Lists top-level (root, non-draft) looms: `listLooms().filter(l => !l.draft && !l.parentLoomId)`. Response `{ looms, active: activeLoomIds() }`.
- Core: `listLooms`, `activeLoomIds`.

#### `POST /api/looms`
File: same as above.
- Starts a new loom — fire-and-forget: `startLoom` persists a queued loom and returns immediately; the executor weaves it in the background.
- Body (`StartLoomInput`):

| Field | Type | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `project` | string | Required, non-empty. |
| `kind` | `"quickfix"\|"story"\|"custom"\|"verify"` | Required, must be one of these four. |
| `prompt` | string | Required, non-empty. |
| `acceptanceCriteria` | string[]? | Each entry must be a trimmed non-empty string. **Required non-empty when `kind === "verify"`** ("a verify loom needs acceptanceCriteria"). |
| `maxAttempts` | integer? | Must be `>= 1` if present. |
| `target` | `"dev"\|"preview"\|"prod"`? | |

- `400` on any validation failure or on a `startLoom` throw (registry/validation error).
- Core: `startLoom`, `listAccounts`, `loadPolicy`, `StartLoomInput` type.

#### `GET /api/looms/[id]`
File: [`apps/web/app/api/looms/[id]/route.ts`](../apps/web/app/api/looms/[id]/route.ts)
- Single loom snapshot. `404` `{error:"Loom not found."}` if missing.
- Core: `getLoom`.

#### `POST /api/looms/[id]/accept`
File: [`apps/web/app/api/looms/[id]/accept/route.ts`](../apps/web/app/api/looms/[id]/accept/route.ts)
- **The human-only "close the loom" action.** Acceptor identity is the literal string `"you"`, hardcoded server-side — **never client-supplied**. This is the code-level enforcement point for "a human always accepts."
- Body (optional, tolerated absent/empty): `{ override?: boolean, missing?: string }`. A clean accept of a `ready` loom sends none. Accepting any other non-`done` state (`queued`, `needs-review`, `blocked`, `failed`, …) requires `{ override: true, missing }` — `acceptLoom` throws (surfaced as `400`) on a bare override without `missing` named. An already-`done` loom or a child loom (`parentLoomId` set, consumed by weave rollup) is also rejected.
- `404` if loom missing. Response `{ ok: true, loom }` on success, `{ error }` (`400`) on `acceptLoom` throw.
- Core: `acceptLoom`, `getLoom`.

#### `POST /api/looms/[id]/block/answer`
File: [`apps/web/app/api/looms/[id]/block/answer/route.ts`](../apps/web/app/api/looms/[id]/block/answer/route.ts)
- Answers a `blocked` loom (adaptive-verification escalation) and re-dispatches the verified build.
- Body: `{ devCommand?, verifyCommand?, servers?, runbook? }` — at least one of `devCommand`/`verifyCommand`/`servers` is required (`400` otherwise). `servers`, if present, must parse against the `ServersConfig` zod schema.
- `404` if loom missing; `400` if `loom.state !== "blocked"`.
- Core: `answerBlocked`, `getLoom`, `listAccounts`, `loadPolicy`, `ServersConfig` schema.

#### `POST /api/looms/[id]/cancel`
File: [`apps/web/app/api/looms/[id]/cancel/route.ts`](../apps/web/app/api/looms/[id]/cancel/route.ts)
- Aborts an in-flight loom (only effective while its process is alive in this server). No body. Response `{ ok: boolean }`.
- Core: `cancelLoom`.

#### `POST /api/looms/[id]/charter/approve`
File: [`apps/web/app/api/looms/[id]/charter/approve/route.ts`](../apps/web/app/api/looms/[id]/charter/approve/route.ts)
- Approves a drafted charter and dispatches the verified execution loop. No body is read at all — only the `id` route param — so the caller cannot supply any state/verdict.
- `404` if loom missing. Acceptor identity `"you"` is server-fixed.
- Core: `approveCharter`, `getLoom`, `listAccounts`, `loadPolicy`.

#### `GET /api/looms/[id]/chat?role=steerer|escalation`
File: [`apps/web/app/api/looms/[id]/chat/route.ts`](../apps/web/app/api/looms/[id]/chat/route.ts)
- Read-only continuity seed for a loom-born chat session (the loom's Chat tab / the escalation "discuss with the orchestrator" surface). Returns the most-recent non-archived chat of the requested role anchored to this loom, shaped as `InitialChat`, or `{ chat: null }`. Never writes.
- Uses `apps/web/lib/store.ts` (`getChat`, `listChats`), core `getLoom`.

#### `GET /api/looms/[id]/events`
File: [`apps/web/app/api/looms/[id]/events/route.ts`](../apps/web/app/api/looms/[id]/events/route.ts)
- SSE poll-tail of a loom, 400ms interval. On first sighting: full loom snapshot as `run`. Each tick: newly appended events (`readEvents`) as `ev`, then a fresh `run` snapshot if `loom.updatedAt` moved. Terminal states (`done|needs-review|halted|failed|skipped`) close the stream with a final `end` event carrying the loom.
- Tolerates the loom directory not existing yet on connect — keeps polling silently.
- Core: `getLoom`, `readEvents`.

#### `GET /api/looms/[id]/evidence/[...path]`
File: [`apps/web/app/api/looms/[id]/evidence/[...path]/route.ts`](../apps/web/app/api/looms/[id]/evidence/[...path]/route.ts)
- Read-only static file serve of a loom's evidence artifacts. Content-Type map: `.png`/`.jpg`/`.jpeg`/`.webp`/`.txt`/`.json`, else `application/octet-stream`.
- **Path-traversal guard**: `target = path.resolve(evidenceDir, ...segments)`; rejects (`403`) if `path.relative(evidenceDir, target)` is empty, starts with `..`, or is absolute. `404` if not a regular file.
- Core: `loomDir`.

#### `POST /api/looms/[id]/reject`
File: [`apps/web/app/api/looms/[id]/reject/route.ts`](../apps/web/app/api/looms/[id]/reject/route.ts)
- Sends a verified/paused/unverified loom back to work with feedback — can never itself reach `done`.
- Body: `{ feedback: string }`, required non-empty. Rejecter identity server-fixed to `"you"`.
- Core: `rejectLoom`, `getLoom`, `listAccounts`, `loadPolicy`.

#### `POST /api/looms/[id]/resume`
File: [`apps/web/app/api/looms/[id]/resume/route.ts`](../apps/web/app/api/looms/[id]/resume/route.ts)
- No-feedback retry of a `failed`/`needs-review`/`blocked` loom back into the same verified loop. No body. Can only land back at `ready`, never `done`.
- Core: `resumeLoom`, `getLoom`, `listAccounts`, `loadPolicy`.

#### `GET /api/looms/[id]/spec/[...path]`
File: [`apps/web/app/api/looms/[id]/spec/[...path]/route.ts`](../apps/web/app/api/looms/[id]/spec/[...path]/route.ts)
- Read-only static file serve of a single Spec Bundle file. Same path-traversal guard pattern as the evidence route, with extra content types (`.md`, `.feature`, `.csv`, `.yaml`, `.yml`).
- Core: `specDir`.

#### `GET /api/looms/[id]/spec`
File: [`apps/web/app/api/looms/[id]/spec/route.ts`](../apps/web/app/api/looms/[id]/spec/route.ts)
- Bundle metadata: file list (internal files `contract.json`/`provenance.json`/`objective.md` filtered out), parsed Verification Contract + parse errors, provenance, objective text.
- `404` if loom missing.
- Core: `bundleVersion`, `listBundleFiles`, `readContract`, `readProvenance`, `readBundleFile`, `getLoom`, `CONTRACT_FILE`, `PROVENANCE_FILE`.

#### `POST /api/looms/[id]/steer`
File: [`apps/web/app/api/looms/[id]/steer/route.ts`](../apps/web/app/api/looms/[id]/steer/route.ts)
- Owner adds a directive from `ready` (or a P5 `needs-review`); re-enters the verified loop, never jumps to `done`.
- Body: `{ directive: string }`, required non-empty. Steerer identity server-fixed.
- Core: `steerLoom`, `getLoom`, `listAccounts`, `loadPolicy`.

#### `GET /api/looms/[id]/threads`
File: [`apps/web/app/api/looms/[id]/threads/route.ts`](../apps/web/app/api/looms/[id]/threads/route.ts)
- Child looms of a woven root (the weaver's parallel threads). Never `404`s — `{ threads: [] }` for a leaf/non-weaving loom.
- Core: `listChildLooms`.

### MCP OAuth

#### `GET /api/mcp/oauth/callback?state=&code=&error=`
File: [`apps/web/app/api/mcp/oauth/callback/route.ts`](../apps/web/app/api/mcp/oauth/callback/route.ts)
- OAuth authorization-server redirect target. Looks up the single-use pending flow by `state` (`takePending`); an unknown/expired state redirects to `/projects` with a generic error (no information leak). On success calls `completeConnect` (validates state, exchanges code, persists the record + mirrors the access token) then redirects to `/projects/[project]/settings?mcpConnected=<server>`. On failure, redirects to `?mcpOAuthError=<server>: <reason>`.
- Core: `completeConnect`. Local: `takePending` (`apps/web/lib/mcp-oauth-pending.ts`).

#### `POST /api/mcp/oauth/connect`
File: [`apps/web/app/api/mcp/oauth/connect/route.ts`](../apps/web/app/api/mcp/oauth/connect/route.ts)
- Starts a browser OAuth connect flow for a project's `http`-transport MCP server. OAuth is **auto-detected, not declared** — works for any `http` server regardless of an `auth` block in the manifest.
- Body: `{ project: string, server: string }`. `404` unknown project or unknown server on that project. `400` if the server's `transport !== "http"`.
- On the "no usable client-identity strategy" failure (`beginConnect` throws containing that string), responds `422` with `{ error, needsClientId: true }` so the UI can prompt for a manual client ID under Configure → Advanced. Any other `beginConnect` failure → `502`.
- Response `{ url: authorizationUrl }` for the client to navigate to.
- Core: `beginConnect`, `getProject`. Local: `putPending` (`apps/web/lib/mcp-oauth-pending.ts`).

#### `POST /api/mcp/oauth/disconnect`
File: [`apps/web/app/api/mcp/oauth/disconnect/route.ts`](../apps/web/app/api/mcp/oauth/disconnect/route.ts)
- Forgets a stored MCP OAuth session — deletes the record and clears the mirrored `mcp:<project>:<server>` token. Idempotent.
- Body: `{ project: string, server: string }`. Response `{ ok: boolean }`.
- Core: `clearMcpToken`, `deleteRecord`.

#### `GET /api/mcp/oauth/status?project=`
File: [`apps/web/app/api/mcp/oauth/status/route.ts`](../apps/web/app/api/mcp/oauth/status/route.ts)
- Per-server connection/detection status for the settings UI: `{ requiresOAuth, connected, expiresAt?, health }` per `http` server (`stdio` servers are omitted). `requiresOAuth` is derived from a concurrent `probeMcpAuth`; `health` from `checkMcpHealth` (authenticated if a token is on file). Both are best-effort — this route never 500s.
- Core: `checkMcpHealth`, `getMcpToken`, `getProject`, `getRecord`, `probeMcpAuth`.

### Projects

#### `GET /api/projects`
File: [`apps/web/app/api/projects/route.ts`](../apps/web/app/api/projects/route.ts)
- Lists registered projects. Response `{ projects }`.
- Core: `listProjects`.

#### `POST /api/projects`
File: same as above.
- Registers an existing telar repo, or scaffolds a fresh `telar.yaml` when `create: true`.
- Body: `{ root: string (required), create?: boolean, manifest?: Partial<ProjectManifest> }`.
- Response `{ manifest }`, or `{ error }` (`400`) on throw.
- Core: `createProject`, `registerProject`.

#### `PATCH /api/projects/[name]`
File: [`apps/web/app/api/projects/[name]/route.ts`](../apps/web/app/api/projects/[name]/route.ts)
- Edits a project's `telar.yaml` in place. `name`/`root` are immutable (`400` if a change to either is attempted). Merges onto the **raw file text**, not the zod-stripped in-memory manifest — so unknown/future YAML fields survive a partial edit — then re-validates the merge with `ProjectManifest.safeParse` before writing.
- Body fields (all optional, conditionally spread so omission never wipes a field): `account` (validated via `getAccount`), `baseBranch`, `adapter`, `devCommand`, `gates`, `mcpServers`, `guardrails` (merged onto existing), `urls` (per-key `dev|preview|prod`; an empty string clears that key).
- **Optimistic concurrency**: re-reads the file immediately before writing and returns `409` ("telar.yaml changed on disk...") if it changed since the initial read.
- Core: `getAccount`, `getProject`, `writeManifest`, `ProjectManifest`. Uses the `yaml` package directly for the raw-text merge.

#### `DELETE /api/projects/[name]`
File: same as above.
- Unregisters a project (leaves the repo/`telar.yaml` untouched). Response `{ ok: boolean }`.
- Core: `unregisterProject`.

#### `GET /api/projects/[name]/commands`
File: [`apps/web/app/api/projects/[name]/commands/route.ts`](../apps/web/app/api/projects/[name]/commands/route.ts)
- Lists custom slash commands scanned from `<root>/.claude/commands/**/*.md`.
- Core: `getProject`. Local: `apps/web/lib/commands.ts` (`listProjectCommands`).

#### `GET /api/projects/[name]/mcp`
File: [`apps/web/app/api/projects/[name]/mcp/route.ts`](../apps/web/app/api/projects/[name]/mcp/route.ts)
- Reports, per declared MCP secret key, whether it's filled — a write-only surface that never returns actual token values. Response `{ tokens: Record<string, boolean> }`.
- Core: `declaredMcpSecretKeys`, `hasMcpToken`.

#### `POST /api/projects/[name]/mcp`
File: same as above.
- Sets a secret token. Body `{ key: string, token: string }`, both required non-empty. Response `{ ok: true }`.
- Core: `setMcpToken`.

#### `DELETE /api/projects/[name]/mcp`
File: same as above.
- Clears a secret token. Body `{ key: string }`. Response `{ ok: boolean }`.
- Core: `clearMcpToken`.

#### Git tab — `apps/web/app/api/projects/[name]/git/**`

All backed by [`apps/web/lib/server/git-tab.ts`](../apps/web/lib/server/git-tab.ts); none imports `@telar/core` beyond `getProject`.

| Route | File | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/projects/[name]/git` | `git/route.ts` | Header + worktrees + branches + commits overview via `buildOverview(root, name, baseBranch)`. `404` unknown project; `500` if `buildOverview` throws. |
| `POST /api/projects/[name]/git/cleanup` | `git/cleanup/route.ts` | Human-triggered worktree/branch removal. Body `{ items: Array<{kind:"worktree", id, force?, confirm?, deleteMergedBranch?} \| {kind:"branch", name}> }`. `400` on malformed items. Uses `runCleanup`. |
| `GET /api/projects/[name]/git/files?path=` | `git/files/route.ts` | One directory level of repo files. `path` validated via `safeRepoDir`; `400` on an invalid/escaping path. Uses `buildFiles`. |
| `GET /api/projects/[name]/git/remote` | `git/remote/route.ts` | `gh` CLI status, auth-gated. **Fails open** — never `500`s; returns `{ connected: false, reason: "gh-error" }` on any `buildRemote` throw (verified: `try { getProject } catch → 404`, then `try { buildRemote } catch → {connected:false}`). Uses `buildRemote`. |
| `POST /api/projects/[name]/git/remote/issues` | `git/remote/issues/route.ts` | Creates a GitHub issue. Body `{ title (required), body? }`. Uses `createIssue`. |
| `GET /api/projects/[name]/git/remote/issues/[number]` | `git/remote/issues/[number]/route.ts` | Issue detail. `number` validated via `parsePositiveInt`. Uses `fetchIssueDetail`. |
| `POST /api/projects/[name]/git/remote/issues/[number]/comment` | `.../comment/route.ts` | Comment on an issue. Body `{ body (required non-empty) }`. Uses `commentIssue`. |
| `POST /api/projects/[name]/git/remote/issues/[number]/state` | `.../state/route.ts` | Close/reopen. Body `{ state: "open"\|"closed" }`. Uses `setIssueState`. |
| `GET /api/projects/[name]/git/remote/prs/[number]` | `git/remote/prs/[number]/route.ts` | PR detail (metadata + reviews + checks + capped file diffs). Uses `fetchPRDetail`. |
| `POST /api/projects/[name]/git/remote/prs/[number]/comment` | `.../comment/route.ts` | Comment on a PR. Body `{ body }`. Uses `commentPR`. |
| `GET /api/projects/[name]/git/remote/prs/[number]/files` | `.../files/route.ts` | Standalone paginated PR file diffs (`FILE_CAP`/`PATCH_CAP`). Uses `fetchPRFiles`. |

*The `git/remote/*` routes uniformly share the "auth-gated, never 500, `{connected:false,reason:"gh-error"}` on any throw" degrade pattern.*

### Ultra (parallel-run harness)

#### `GET /api/ultra`
File: [`apps/web/app/api/ultra/route.ts`](../apps/web/app/api/ultra/route.ts)
- Lists every Ultra run across every session, newest-first, self-healing (a manifest still claiming `running` with no live task in this process reconciles to `stopped` on read). Response `{ runs }`.

File: same as above.

- Body: `{ script: string (required), args?, project: string (required, resolved via getProject), account? (resolved via getAccount), sessionId?, messageId? }`.
- `400` on any validation/compile-reject (`launchUltra`'s `!result.ok` path returns `{ error: result.error }`, `400` — the same shape as every other validation failure on this route; a richer structured reject surfaced to the authoring agent is a concern of the `ultra` MCP tool wrapper, not this route).
- Response `{ runId, meta }`.
- Core: `getAccount`, `getProject`, `launchUltra`, `AccountProfile` type.

File: [`apps/web/app/api/ultra/[id]/route.ts`](../apps/web/app/api/ultra/[id]/route.ts)

- One spawned agent's transcript (text/tool/tool-result/result events), tagged with retry `attempt`. `ordinal` must be a non-negative integer (`400` otherwise). Never `404`s — an unsettled/nonexistent ordinal just returns an empty array.
- Core: `readUltraAgentTranscript`.

#### `GET /api/ultra/[id]/events`
File: [`apps/web/app/api/ultra/[id]/events/route.ts`](../apps/web/app/api/ultra/[id]/events/route.ts)

## Streaming Protocols

None of the streaming routes use the Vercel AI SDK's data-stream protocol — every one is a hand-rolled `text/event-stream` response built directly from a `ReadableStream`, with headers `Content-Type: text/event-stream`, `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-transform`, `Connection: keep-alive`. There are **5 SSE endpoints** in total, in three distinct shapes:

### 1. Chat turn stream — `POST /api/chat`
The richest protocol: 16 named event types (`session`, `saved`, `thinking`, `thinking_delta`, `delta`, `text`, `tool`, `tool_result`, `task_status`, `permission`, `permission_result`, `permission_denied`, `error`, `interrupted`, `done`, `title`), each written as a standard named SSE frame:
```
event: <name>
data: <json>

```
Frames are emitted live as the SDK/Codex bridge streams (`stream_event` → `delta`/`thinking_delta`; `system:init` → `session`; tool-use blocks → `tool`/`tool_result`; interactive permission prompts → `permission`; the terminal SDK result → `done`). The stream ends when the turn naturally completes, is stopped via `POST /api/chat/stop`, or the client disconnects (in which case persistence still runs server-side in a `finally` block).

### 2. Reconnect-tail of a chat turn — `GET /api/chat/[sessionId]/events`
Not a separate protocol so much as a **replay** of protocol 1's own event names: a reconnecting client gets the same `session`/`delta`/`tool`/… frames the original `POST /api/chat` caller saw, sourced from an append-only per-session log file plus a bounded in-memory delta ring for the current in-flight text block, polled every 300ms. A `closed` event (if present in the log) ends the stream. Silently emits nothing and closes if the turn isn't currently live (anti-double-render — the page already has the completed turn from `chats.json`).

### 3. Poll-tail of a long-running entity — `GET /api/looms/[id]/events`, `GET /api/ultra/[id]/events`
Identical shape on both routes, polled at 400ms:
- `run` — full entity snapshot (Loom or Ultra manifest), sent on first sighting and again whenever `updatedAt` changes.
- `ev` — each newly appended line from the entity's append-only event log (`readEvents`/`readUltraEvents`), drained in order.
- `end` — sent once with the final snapshot when the entity reaches a terminal state (looms: `done|needs-review|halted|failed|skipped`; Ultra runs: `done|failed|stopped`), then the stream closes.

Both tolerate the backing directory/file not existing yet at connect time — they keep polling silently rather than erroring, so a client can subscribe to an id the instant it's minted, before the executor has written anything to disk.

### 4. Provider login stream — `GET /api/accounts/[name]/login`
The **odd one out**: frames are written as bare `data: <json>\n\n` with **no `event:` field** (default SSE `message` event), one frame per item yielded by `@telar/core`'s `session.events` async iterator (from `spawnProviderLogin`), plus a synthetic `{ type: "failed", error }` frame on throw. Event discrimination happens entirely inside the JSON payload's own `type` field, not the SSE `event:` line — a client must parse every `data:` frame and branch on `.type`, unlike the other four routes where the SSE `event:` line itself is the discriminator.

## Authentication & Errors

**Authentication**: None. There is no `middleware.ts` in `apps/web`, and no route reads a session cookie, bearer token, or API key. Every route trusts its caller unconditionally — this is architecturally a local single-operator cockpit (see [`../apps/desktop`](../apps/desktop), which boots this same Next.js server inside an Electron `BrowserWindow` pointed at `localhost`). The only credential-shaped flows in this surface are:
- **Provider login** (`GET/POST/DELETE /api/accounts/[name]/login`) — authenticates the *server process* to Anthropic/OpenAI on the user's behalf; it is not app-level auth.
- **MCP OAuth** (`/api/mcp/oauth/**`) — authenticates the server to a *project-declared* MCP server; also not app-level auth.

**Human-accept moat**: enforced at this HTTP layer, not just the UI. `POST /api/looms/[id]/accept` hardcodes the acceptor identity to `"you"` server-side — no request body field can override who "accepted." `POST /api/chat`'s `PreToolUse` hook (`preToolUseGuardrail`, inline in `apps/web/app/api/chat/route.ts`) force-routes `mcp__loom__start_loom` and `mcp__loom__answer_blocked` through the interactive permission card in **every** `permissionMode`, including `auto`/`acceptEdits` — defeating an attempted client-side bypass of the "always ask before committing/answering" rule. No route anywhere exposes an agent-callable "accept" or "done" action; `getLoom`'s state machine only reaches `done` via the human-bound accept route.

**Error shape**: `{ error: string }` on nearly every failure, occasionally extended: `{ error, needsClientId: true }` (`POST /api/mcp/oauth/connect`, `422`), `{ ok: false }` (permission/watch-cancel soft-failures, `200`). A few routes return a plain-text body instead of JSON on `404` (e.g. `GET /api/chats/[id]` → `"not found"`; the loom `evidence`/`spec` static-serve routes → `"Forbidden"`/`"Not Found"`).

**Status code conventions** (observed across all 56 route files):

| Code | Meaning | Representative routes |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | Success | All happy paths. |
| `204` | Success, no body | `DELETE /api/chats/[id]`. |
| `400` | Validation failure, or a wrapped domain-layer throw (`@telar/core` functions like `acceptLoom`/`startLoom`/`launchUltra` throw on invalid state transitions; routes catch and re-surface as `400`). | Nearly every `POST`/`PATCH` with a body. |
| `403` | Path-traversal guard tripped | `GET /api/looms/[id]/evidence/[...path]`, `GET /api/looms/[id]/spec/[...path]`. |
| `404` | Entity not found (project, account, loom, chat, MCP server) | Most `[id]`/`[name]` routes. |
| `409` | Conflict — already logged in, already resolved/no session, or a stale concurrent `telar.yaml` edit | `GET/POST /api/accounts/[name]/login`, `PATCH /api/projects/[name]`. |
| `422` | Actionable client follow-up needed (not a hard failure) | `POST /api/mcp/oauth/connect` (`needsClientId`). |
| `500` | Unhandled server-side exception | `GET /api/projects/[name]/git` (`buildOverview` throw), `openInTerminal`'s `osascript` spawn failure. |
| `501` | Platform not supported | `POST /api/browse` outside macOS. |
| `502` | Upstream/dependency failure | `POST /api/mcp/oauth/connect` (non-client-id `beginConnect` failures). |

**Fail-open exception**: the entire `GET /api/projects/[name]/git/remote/**` family deliberately never returns `500` for a `gh` CLI failure — it returns `200` with `{ connected: false, reason: "gh-error" }` so the UI's GitHub panel degrades to "not connected" rather than surfacing a hard error for an optional integration.
